plate.narration: In MossHome, a tree door swings open above a mat of welcome moss. A bigfoot archivist waits with an armful of knotted cords. Root stairs twist upward behind her. This town keeps its stories in surprising places.

objectives.label: Read the spiral in the path archive
Earned the trust of MossHome's record

goal.text: Find out what the forest town remembers, then climb out to the foothills.

steps.label: Climb up out of the forest

facet_confiscated.name: The Confiscated Stone
facet_confiscated.text: The loudest stone in the forest's pile. MossHome's record knows who is carrying it.

knot_cord.name: MossHome Knot-Cord
knot_cord.text: Old bigfoot knots that say the record knows you. Show it when the forest pays back.

scene_mosshome.narration: MossHome is a town that was grown instead of built: houses that are hollow trees, staircases that are roots, windows of woven leaves. In the square, a chair has grown wrong. It leans. A little sign beside it says FILE OPENED. The bigfoot runner from the woods jogs past with a fresh bundle of cords, waves without stopping, and shouts, "You found it! Welcome to MossHome! Our archive remembers every path in the Woods. Go and find out what it remembers, then take the high paths up to the foothills!"

choices.label: Act out your road, and ask to see the archive
Wipe your feet on the welcome moss before you even knock
Ask the archive door first, the MossHome way
Mention that the worst glade is green again

scene_mosshome_feet.narration: Before anybody knocks, you wipe your feet on the welcome moss by the archive door. Then, to be safe, you wipe them again. The door flies open. An archivist stands there with her hand over her heart. "Twice," she breathes. "Nobody from outside ever wipes twice." She lets you straight in, and tells two other archivists about it on the way.

choices.label: Go in, feet spotless

scene_mosshome_glade_word.narration: You mention the glade. The archivist at the door goes still, then pulls a cord from her belt and runs her thumb along it to a knot near the end. "That glade," she says. "The path record changed this morning. It got better." She looks at you as if you have just handed her a book she has been waiting for. "In. Feet."

choices.label: Go in

scene_mosshome_ask_door.narration: Your bigfoot walks up to the archive door and knocks on it, three slow knocks, the way MossHome children are taught before they can walk. The door opens by itself. Behind it, an archivist drops a whole armful of cords and says, "Nobody's done that in years. Come in. Wipe your feet."

choices.label: Go in

check_archive_door.narration: The archivist folds her arms on the doorstep. "Don't tell me your road," she says. "Show me. Every path that moved under your boots." The welcome moss is springy and does not mind being stomped on.

interaction.cue: Everybody act out a piece of your road, until the archivist's eyebrows go up.

options.label: Stomp a squelchy marsh
options.reaction: Squelch, squelch. The archivist's eyebrow twitches.

options.label: Splash across a river
options.reaction: Splash! A drop lands on the archivist's clipboard.

options.label: Tiptoe past grumpy thorns
options.reaction: You tiptoe so well that the moss holds its breath.

onSuccess.narration: You stomp the last bend of your road into the moss. The archivist's eyebrows go up, and then up again. "Oh," she says. "Oh, come in. Wipe your feet. Wipe them twice."

onFailure.narration: Halfway through, you stomp the wrong way and sit down hard in the moss. "Wait on the bench," says the archivist. The bench is still growing. Very slowly, over the next hour, it lifts you up to the window, and you see the table anyway.

scene_archive_table.narration: The archive table is one slice of an enormous tree, with every path in the Woods drawn on it in moss-ink. All season the archivists have been marking every path the Woods has moved since the mountain went off. Each change is pinned with a little thorn, and there are a great many thorns.

choices.label: Read the path records yourself
Help plot the moved paths with pins and yarn
Ask to see the newest thorns

scene_archive_table_read.narration: Your bigfoot leans over the table and reads it the way MossHome children learn to: one finger along the moss-ink, humming each path's name. The archivist stops fussing about feet altogether. The finger goes around, and around, and around again, and your bigfoot goes very quiet, because the shape is already there under the finger.

choices.label: Say what you see

scene_archive_table_newest.narration: The archivist points to the freshest thorns, still green. A path that folded itself up three times in one morning. A hedge that held three prospectors by the coat-tails. A beech that sat down across a path and asked a question. "Somebody walked through all of those this week," she says, and looks at your boots. "Somebody with marsh mud on."

choices.label: Step back and look at the whole table

check_plot.narration: The archivist hands you a ball of yarn and a fistful of thorns. "Three paths moved in the first week," she says. "Pin them in the order they moved, and the shape will show itself. The archive remembers a little. Put your memories together."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then pin the three moved paths in the order they moved.
clues: The river path moved first, on the morning of the big rumble.
The tree path moved after the marsh path.

onSuccess.narration: Thorn, yarn, thorn, yarn, and slowly a shape comes out of it.

onFailure.narration: You tangle the yarn so thoroughly a cat would be embarrassed. An archivist untangles it with one finger and shows you the shape anyway.

scene_spiral.narration: Plotted on the table, the moved paths are not random at all. They spiral, around and around every place a stone fell, like bathwater going down the drain, every path bending away. It is what the land has been saying all the way north. The Woods is not flinching from the mountain. It is flinching from the stones.

choices.label: Ask if this has ever happened before
Tell them the stones hum, and hum the note
Pin your own road onto the table
Hold the witch's tuned charm over the table

scene_spiral_on.narration: "Before?" The archivist looks at the others. Nobody answers. Then one of them goes, very quietly, to the back of the archive, and after a while you hear slow footsteps coming back, and a small bird singing, getting closer, as if the footsteps have brought their own music.

choices.label: Wait for the footsteps

scene_spiral_hum.narration: You hum the note, the one the stones hum. Every archivist in the room stops. One drops a whole spool of cord, and it rolls away under the table, unwinding, and nobody chases it. "That note," says the archivist, very quietly. "The oldest knots were tied to that note." Then she will not say another word until somebody fetches the oldest archivist.

choices.label: Wait for the oldest archivist

scene_spiral_pin.narration: You take a thorn and pin your own road: through river and marsh, into the trees. Your thread runs right past three of the spiral's middles. The archivists lean in. "You walked the edge of it all the way," one says. "No wonder the paths noticed you." She ties a knot to remember it, then sends for the oldest archivist.

choices.label: Wait for the oldest archivist

scene_spiral_charm.narration: You hold the witch's charm over the table and move it slowly across. Over every middle of every spiral it rings, ding, ding, ding, like a finger tapping a map. Between them it is silent. The archivists go pale under their fur. Then they send, quickly, for the oldest archivist, who does not like to be sent for quickly.

choices.label: Wait for the oldest archivist

scene_knot_cords.narration: The oldest archivist, whose beard has a bird's nest in it (occupied), brings out a box of cords tied in knots: records so old they were never written down. "The paths flinched like this once before," he says. "Long, long ago." The knots are worn smooth from hands that kept checking. And the stones, he adds, are older than the mountain's name. The unicorns are right.

choices.label: Ask what the forest does with the stones it takes
Thank him, and go and rest

scene_knot_cords_rest.narration: You thank him and turn to go. Behind you, the oldest archivist tells a very old cord, not quite quietly enough, "Didn't ask where the forest keeps what it takes. Good manners, or no curiosity." The archivist walking you out stops in the doorway, sighs, and turns around. "You'll want to know where the forest keeps what it takes," she says. "Everybody does, in the end."

choices.label: Ask about the pile, then

scene_pile_question.narration: The archivists look at each other. Yes, the forest keeps a pile: everything the Woods has taken off careless treasure hunters, heaped up somewhere secret. Yes, they know where it is. No, they will not say. "The pile is the forest's," says one. "We only keep the record. And the record decides who it trusts."

choices.label: Ask the record to trust you
Tell them the worst glade is green again
Follow the archivist who keeps glancing at the back door
Let it be. It's the forest's pile.

check_trust.prompt: Tell the archivists, honestly, what you want the stones for

onSuccess.narration: They listen to the whole thing. Then they all write something down at once, and the oldest one nods.

onFailure.narration: "The record doesn't know you yet," says the archivist, kindly, and closes the box. Maybe it will, by the time you're further north.

scene_pile_visit.narration: Behind MossHome, in a hollow under the roots, is the pile: pickaxes, sieves, three hats and a heap of humming gems. One stone hums louder than all the rest. "That one wants to go north," says the archivist. "You're going north. Carry it, if you like. The record will know who has it."

choices.label: Carry the stone north
Leave it with the forest

scene_pile_visit_leave.narration: You leave the loud stone where the forest put it. The archivist does not look surprised. She ties a small knot in a cord anyway, a different knot, and says, "The record will remember that too." Behind you the pile hums on in the dark, keeping itself company.

choices.label: Go and rest

scene_pile_visit_carry.narration: You lift the loud stone out of the pile. It hums against your chest like a cat that has decided you will do. The archivist ties a small knot in a cord and does not say what it means. "North," she says. "That's all it wants."

choices.label: Go and rest

scene_pile_sneak.narration: Your kitsune slips after the archivist like a shadow with a tail: through a back door, down a root-stair, into a hollow full of pickaxes, hats and humming gems. One stone sings louder than the rest. Nobody is watching. Nobody except, possibly, the entire forest.

choices.label: Pocket the loud stone
Remember where it is, and leave it

scene_pile_sneak_leave.narration: Your kitsune looks at the loud stone for a long moment, memorizes exactly where it is, and leaves it there. On the way back up the root-stair, a root moves out of the way to make the step easier. It did not do that on the way down.

choices.label: Slip back out

scene_pile_sneak_pocket.narration: Your kitsune pockets the loud stone with the smoothest hand in the realm. Nobody sees. Then every root in the hollow creaks at once, very softly, like a very large person clearing its throat. Nobody saw. The forest saw.

choices.label: Slip back out

scene_leaning_chair.narration: Crossing the square toward the guest trees, you pass the leaning chair again. Now that you have seen the spiral, you know what to look for. It is not leaning at random. It is leaning away from something, the way the mosshorns stepped away from the gem cart. A small archivist is measuring it with a string, and sighing.

choices.label: Sit in it and try to lean it back upright
Work out what it's leaning away from

check_chair_sit.narration: The small archivist with the string waves you over. "It will not stand up for one person," she says. "One of you sits and leans, and the rest push on the back. The chair has to feel all of you."

interaction.cue: Friends push the chair upright while one of you sits and leans back.

onSuccess.narration: You sit and lean back hard. With a long creak the chair comes upright, and holds, and holds, and the moment you stand up it leans straight back again, slowly, like a sunflower turning. The small archivist writes on her sign, under FILE OPENED: STILL OPEN.

onFailure.narration: You sit, and lean, and the chair politely tips you out onto the moss, the way you would tip out a cat that has sat on your homework. The small archivist laughs so hard she drops her string. "It does that to everybody," she says. "Even the Eldest. Especially the Eldest."

scene_leaning_chair_follow.narration: You stand behind the chair and look where its back is pointing. It leans away from the root-stairs behind the archive, the ones that go down into the dark under the town. The small archivist sees you looking, and very carefully goes and stands in front of the root-stairs, humming, as if she has always wanted to stand exactly there.

choices.label: Pretend you did not notice

rest_guest_tree.narration: MossHome puts you up in a guest tree. The hammocks hum lullabies if you rock them, and the moss tea tastes like a rainy afternoon, in a good way. Rest, and think about what you know now.

choices.label: Go and see the elders
Help the runner tie the day's cords first
Rock in a humming hammock until it sings you to sleep

rest_guest_tree_knot.narration: The runner is sitting on the guest tree's root, still jogging her feet, tying the day's cords. She shows you a MossHome knot: over, under, twist, and pull. "Holds a bridge plank," she puffs. "Holds a promise. Holds a whole path in the record." It takes you nine tries. On the tenth, she cheers so loudly a hammock wakes up.

choices.label: Go and see the elders

rest_guest_tree_hammock.narration: You climb into a hammock and rock it, and it hums, a low, slow lullaby that sounds a lot like rain on leaves. You mean to rock for just a minute. When you wake, it is morning, there is moss tea on a little shelf beside you, and somebody's hammock is still humming, very softly, a little out of tune.

choices.label: Go and see the elders

scene_runners_post.narration: On the way to the elders you pass the runners' post, a hollow stump where MossHome runners drop off their cords and pick up new ones. Three runners have just come in from very far away, steaming, still jogging on the spot. They carry news from the other roads north, and everybody wants to hear it. You get to ask first.

choices.label: Ask for news from the rush road
Ask for news from the river road
Ask if there is any word from Gullet the ferrywoman

scene_runners_post_rush.narration: "The rush road?" A runner puffs out the news. A ford queue two days long. A witch whose charms ring by themselves. Cinder wolves that won't sleep near the gem wagons. And a soup line, very kind, that keeps asking people about the mountain. "Same shape as here," she says. "Different country. Everybody's noticing."

choices.label: Go on to the elders' ring

scene_runners_post_river.narration: "The river road?" A runner wipes his brow. A stone troll at Stone Crossing has stopped asking riddles. All its tolls are one question now: where did you get that, and where is it going? And out east, the manticore prides are bending their roads around something they won't name. "Everybody's noticing," he puffs. "Nobody's telling."

choices.label: Go on to the elders' ring

scene_runners_post_gullet.narration: "Gullet?" A runner laughs. "Notched hat, hums a lot?" He has news from the marsh: Gullet has run out of hat. She has started on her other hat. And the ribbon crew moved the wisp line out twice more this week. "She said to tell anybody who asked," he puffs, "that she is not worried. Which means she is."

choices.label: Go on to the elders' ring

scene_cloud_gatherer.narration: On the way to the elders, you find a little patch of cloud sitting in the middle of the square, as if it came down the high paths and got lost. In it, on a root, with her tail wrapped around her knees, is a young dragonling with a gathering bag. "I'm not lost," she says at once. "Grandmother sent me to ask your elders something." A flock of embermoths drifts past, glowing, heading south, away from the mountain. She stares. "They never go that way."

choices.label: Walk her to the elders' ring with you
Follow the embermoths a little way to see where they go
Greet her the gathering way

scene_cloud_gatherer_walk.narration: You walk her across the square together. On the way she tells you the one rule, the way every dragonling learns it: "Take what the mountain drops. Never pry at what it holds." She says it twice, to be sure you have it. "The grandmothers say it at the boundary stones. Nobody listens this year." At the elders' ring she sits on the last stump, to wait her turn.

choices.label: Sit down with the elders

check_follow_moths.prompt: Keep up with a drifting flock of embermoths through the trees

onSuccess.narration: You follow them, the gatherer at your heels, to the edge of town, where the whole flock has settled on a fence. Every single moth is facing away from the mountain, like people with their backs to a cold draft. "I'm telling my grandmother," the gatherer whispers. Then she leads you back to the elders' ring.

onFailure.narration: The moths vanish into the trees, glowing, and you lose them. Then they come drifting back past you the other way, as if they have changed their minds, and then change them again. "Even they don't know where to go," says the gatherer, and leads you back to the elders' ring.

scene_cloud_gatherer_greet.narration: Your dragonling touches a claw to their brow and recites the gatherer's greeting: "What the mountain drops, we keep. What it holds, we leave." The young gatherer's whole face lights up. "You're from the foothills!" She sticks to your side all the way to the elders' ring, naming every tree, and tells you her town's bell tower is the tallest in the foothills.

choices.label: Sit down with the elders

choice_elders.narration: The MossHome elders sit in a ring of tree stumps, sipping tea. "You have the outline of it now," says the eldest. "The stones are older than the mountain, and the land has been keeping records. Somebody must be told." She counts on her fingers. "The Skywardens, the guards in silver and violet up at Redspire Citadel, who write everything down. Or the dragonling grandmothers in the foothills, like our young visitor's, who gather what the mountain drops and ring the bells. Tell whoever you like first." She sips. "Only tell us second." Who will you tell? Everybody vote.

choices.label: The Skywardens at Redspire Citadel
The dragonling grandmothers in the foothills
Nobody yet. Keep it close.

choice_elders_close.narration: "Nobody yet," says the eldest, and looks at you over her cup for a long time. "Careful," she says at last. "Careful is a kind of telling, too." She sips. "When you do tell. Second."

choices.label: Go and pack

choice_elders_gatherers.narration: "The gatherer grandmothers," says the eldest, and for the first time all evening she smiles. "They ring the bells in every foothill town, and bells carry further than cords." She sips. "Tell them we said so. And tell us second."

choices.label: Go and pack

choice_elders_wardens.narration: "The wardens," says the eldest, and sips. "They write things down. That is not nothing." She sips again. "Second," she reminds you, and the whole ring of elders nods at once, which makes the tea in every cup ripple.

choices.label: Go and pack

scene_runner.narration: The runner grins and presses the knotted cord into your hands, still warm from carrying. "For later," she says. "When the forest pays back what it took, it'll want to see this. It means the record knows you." Then she's off again, at a jog, because MossHome runners never walk anywhere.

choices.label: Tie it somewhere safe, and set off

scene_falls_stair.narration: The way out of MossHome climbs the falls stair, and the falls are in a mood. Water is running over steps that should be dry, and a bigfoot flood-warden in very tall boots is standing right in it, frowning at a pole marked with notches. "Rising," she says. "Then falling. All day. In time with the mountain's grumbles. Never seen that before."

choices.label: Help her drag stepping logs across the stair
Watch the pole and count the rises with her
Tell her you washed up dripping on the flooded paths
Have a thornguard plant a post in the flood to hold on to

check_falls_logs.prompt: Everybody drag heavy stepping logs across the flooded stair

onSuccess.narration: Heave, roll, heave, and three logs settle across the flooded steps like a little bridge. The flood-warden stamps on each one, hard, and nods. "Proper work," she says, which from a flood-warden is a medal. You cross with dry boots, and she waves you up toward the high paths.

onFailure.narration: A log rolls the wrong way and you sit down in the falls with a splash. The flood-warden hauls you out with one hand, sets you on the top step, and says, "Happens every season. Not usually to this many." Then she drags the logs across herself, as if they weigh nothing at all.

scene_falls_stair_count.narration: You stand with her and watch the pole. The mountain grumbles, far off, and the water climbs a notch. It goes quiet, and the water drops. Grumble, rise. Quiet, fall. Like breathing. The flood-warden writes it all on a cord and ties it to your pack. "For whoever you're telling," she says. "Tell them the water knows too."

choices.label: Climb the stair, carefully

scene_falls_stair_dripping.narration: "The flooded paths?" The flood-warden's whole face cracks into a grin. "You're the soggy ones! The whole forest heard about you!" She laughs, a big bigfoot laugh that echoes off the falls, and then she scoops you up and carries you across the worst of the steps like laundry, and sets you down dry at the top. "Mind you stay that way," she says.

choices.label: Climb on, still dry

scene_soup_tent.narration: Where the high paths begin, there's a little tent selling nothing and giving away soup. The woman ladling it is very kind, with a mask pushed up on her head and DEEP HOLLOW stitched small on her apron. Her name is Marigold. "The world's rules are broken," she says gently. "Whatever sleeps under that mountain could fix them. We're collecting, to help it wake." She rattles a little box.

choices.label: Have some soup, and say nothing
Say no, kindly but firmly
Drop some coins in her box to help it wake

scene_soup_tent_coins.narration: You drop a few coins in the box. They do not clink. The box is lined with something soft, and Marigold's whole face lights up as if you have handed her the sun. "Thank you," she whispers. "It'll wake so gently." You walk on with your hands feeling oddly empty.

choices.label: Up the high paths

scene_soup_tent_refuse.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly but firmly. She nods as if she expected it. "Soup's still soup," she says, and ladles you some anyway, and you take it, because it is cold up here and she is right. The box stays where it is.

choices.label: Up the high paths

scene_soup_tent_soup.narration: You have the soup. It is very good soup. Marigold watches you eat with great kindness and says nothing more, and when you hand the bowls back she has somehow already washed them. The little box rattles once as you go, on its own.

choices.label: Up the high paths

choice_rope_bridge.narration: The high paths begin with a rope bridge over a gorge so deep the river at the bottom looks like a bit of string. Halfway across, two planks are missing. A bigfoot sign at the start says, in careful letters, MIND THE GAP. Underneath, somebody else has added: IT IS A BIG GAP. How will you cross? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Carry a spare plank out to fill the gap
Go hand over hand along the side rope past the gap
Rig a new plank with the runner's knot
Have a duskrunner dart out and scout the gap

check_bridge_test.narration: A stack of spare planks is tied to the bridge rail, with a tag: TAKE ONE, CARRY IT LEVEL, LAY IT OVER THE GAP. The bridge sways, and so does the plank. Every pair of hands has to keep its end steady.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your end until the plank is level, then carry it to the gap.

onSuccess.narration: Step by careful step you carry the plank out, and lay it across the gap with a soft thump. Everybody crosses without a single wobble. On the far side, you add a line under the sign: WE MINDED IT.

onFailure.narration: The plank wobbles, and so do you, and it lands in the gap crooked. It creaks. You say AAH. Then it turns out to be perfectly fine, just a very dramatic plank. You cross with hearts thumping, and laugh about it all the way to the other side.

check_bridge_rope.prompt: Swing hand over hand along the side rope past the missing planks

onSuccess.narration: Hand, hand, hand, and swing your feet onto the far planks. One after another you go over the gap like monkeys, and the bridge hardly sways. A bigfoot coming the other way stops to clap, very slowly, with enormous hands.

onFailure.narration: Halfway along, your arms get tired and you dangle for a moment, like a sock on a clothesline, until the others reach out and pull you in by the belt. Nobody looks down. Well, one person looks down, once, and decides never to do that again.

choice_rope_bridge_knot.narration: Over, under, twist, and pull. You tie a spare plank into the gap with the knot the runner taught you, and it holds like it grew there. A bigfoot coming the other way stops, inspects your knot, tugs it twice, and nods. "MossHome knot," he says. "Somebody taught you right." You cross like it is a garden path.

choices.label: Cross over

scene_halfway_hut.narration: Halfway up the high paths stands a stone hut with a mossy roof, and an old bigfoot path-keeper sitting outside it with a book open on his knees. "Visitors' book," he says proudly. "Everybody who goes up, signs, so I know who to go looking for if they don't come down. Been kept since before MossHome had a name." The book is enormous. The oldest pages are not written at all. They are knotted.

choices.label: Sign your names in the book
Read back through the oldest pages
Buy a honeycake from the keeper's shelf (2 coins)

scene_halfway_hut_sign.narration: You sign your names, in your best writing. The path-keeper reads them out loud, slowly, as if he is tasting them. Then he turns back a few pages and shows you a long column of names from this season, all going up, more than in any year he can remember. "Busy mountain," he says, and blows on your ink to dry it.

choices.label: Climb on

check_hut_pages.prompt: Untangle the oldest knotted pages of the visitors' book without pulling a single knot loose

onSuccess.narration: Back and back you turn, past ink, past scratches, to the knots. Each knot is a climber, and the little knots tied on after are what they met on the way up. The commonest one, by far, means CROSS ANIMALS: THROW THEM A SNACK. The path-keeper taps it. "Still good advice," he says. "There are wolves up there today."

onFailure.narration: The knotted pages are like trying to read a knitted sweater. You turn it upside down and it makes even less sense. The path-keeper chuckles, closes the book, and pours you a cup of something hot. "Takes forty years to read those," he says. "I've done thirty-one."

scene_high_paths.narration: The bigfoot high paths climb along the cliffs above the falls, all rope bridges and stone steps worn into bowls. Halfway up, three cinder wolves are lying across the path, glowing faintly, as if the mountain kicked them out. They aren't hunting. They're cross. And they're in the way.

choices.label: Throw them something easier to chase
Slip past them quickly
Take the hidden high path the wolves don't know
Stand tall and make them go around

scene_high_paths_hidden.narration: Your bigfoot points to a crack in the cliff that looks like nothing at all. It is a path, an old MossHome one, worn into the rock and hidden behind a curtain of ivy. You squeeze along it in single file, right past the wolves' noses, and not one of them so much as twitches an ear. Above you, the trees are thinning out.

choices.label: Climb on to the top

check_distract.prompt: Give three cross wolves something more interesting than you

onSuccess.narration: You lob a handful of jerky from your packs down the slope. Three wolves look at each other, then at the jerky, and decide jerky wins.

onFailure.narration: A strip of jerky bounces off a wolf's nose. The wolf does not find this funny.

check_dash.prompt: Dash past three cinder wolves on a narrow cliff path

onSuccess.narration: Over a rope bridge, under a ledge, and gone before a single wolf has finished yawning.

onFailure.narration: The rope bridge squeaks. Six glowing ears turn around.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves get up, shake off a shower of sparks, and come down the switchback at you.

onVictory.narration: The wolves decide this path isn't worth it and lope off downhill, still grumbling, trailing sparks like a sneeze.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves chase you off the path and down into a gully, and by the time they lose interest, your packs are scattered across half the hillside.

check_regroup.prompt: Gather up your scattered packs before it gets dark

onSuccess.narration: You find everything, even the sock nobody wanted back, and climb on, late but whole.

onFailure.narration: You find one pack, half of another, and a hat that is not yours. The light goes while you are still looking, and somewhere above you a wolf grumbles at the mountain as if it has lost something too.

scene_foothills_view.narration: At the top of the high paths the forest stops and the foothills begin, red and rumbling, falling away to the east. Far off, on top of everything, sits Mount Red Sky with smoke curling off it like a question mark. Somewhere down there are the citadel, the truth, and whatever comes next.

choices.label: Make camp on the flat rock
Climb the lookout rock first

scene_foothills_view_lookout.narration: You scramble up the lookout rock as the sun goes down. From the top you can see the whole of the foothills: the dragonling towns with their bell towers, a citadel of red stone with tiny lights coming on in its windows, and the rush, a long glittering line of lanterns, crawling toward the mountain. Somewhere down there, the young gatherer is on her way home to her grandmother.

choices.label: Climb down and make camp

ending_foothills_rim.narration: You camp on a flat rock at the edge of the foothills, with the forest behind you and the knot-cord safe in somebody's pocket. The mountain grumbles in its sleep all night, like a giant with indigestion. Tomorrow you go down to meet it.

ending_long_way_round.narration: By the time you have found most of your things it is dark, and the wolves are grumbling somewhere above you. You make a cold camp in the gully and come down into the foothills the long way around, a day late and one sock short. The mountain did not wait for you.

interaction_post_relay.narration: Before you can leave the runners' post, a steaming runner thrusts a bundle of knotted cords at you. "Pass them down the stump!" she pants. "Hand to hand! The news has to reach the far runner before the dew dries, and we have run out of legs!"

interaction.cue: Catch the bundle of cords, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: The cords fly from hand to hand and reach the far runner with a whole breath to spare. "Post fee!" she calls, and tosses you three coins, jingling. Then she jogs off with the news, still jogging.

onFailure.narration: One bundle lands in a puddle, and two cords tie themselves to a runner's boot. She hops, laughs, and untangles it. "The news will get there," she says. "News always does."

onAssisted.narration: A runner jogs in between you and takes every other throw. The cords reach the far end in good time, and a runner tosses you three coins, jingling, for the help.

interaction_cord_knots.narration: As you pack, the runner from the square jogs up, tying a cord as she goes. She holds it out. "Watch my hands," she says. "Then tie it back the same way, loop for loop. The record likes to know you can."

interaction.cue: Watch the knots light up, then tie them back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Loop, twist, pull, loop. Your cord comes out exactly like hers, and the runner whoops. "Not one wrong knot!" she says. "I will tell the record."

onFailure.narration: Your knots come out in a tangle shaped like a very confused spider. The runner unties it with one finger. "Close," she says kindly. "I will do the last loop for you."

scene_hut_honeycake.narration: You put two coins in the path-keeper's tin. He takes a honeycake off the shelf behind him, wraps it in a leaf, and hands it over as if it were a medal. "My sister bakes them," he says. "Still warm, if you hurry. Mind the path past the hut. There is a stream, and a young river drake has moved into it."

choices.label: Climb on, with cake

scene_drake_ford.narration: Just past the hut, the high path runs into a stream that tumbles down off the cliff to feed the falls. The only way up is along its stepping stones, and a young river drake has moved in. It is the size of a pony, and it is slapping the water with its tail to make waves, one after another. It does not look mean. It looks like someone whose house the mountain keeps shaking, and who has decided that this stream is the one thing still its own.

choices.label: Hop up the stones between the waves

interaction_stones.narration: Slap! A wave rolls down the stream. Slap! Another. The drake is not aiming at you, but the stones are slick and the waves are big. There is a gap between each one, if you watch for it.

interaction.cue: Wait for the wave to pass, then tap to hop up the stones.

onSuccess.narration: Wave, gap, hop. Wave, gap, hop. You reach the top stone with dry boots, and the drake blinks at you in surprise.

onFailure.narration: You go one hop too early and a wave fills your boots. You scramble up the last stones anyway, squelching, and the drake looks at you as if you have taken its towel.

scene_drake_bank.narration: At the top, the path leaves the stones and follows the streambed itself, a narrow rocky slot with the drake wallowing right in the middle of it. It huffs a puff of steam like a teakettle. It will not move, and it will not let anyone squeeze by, not you, and not anybody else who climbs this path after you. "Mine," its snort says. There is no way around. The drake will have to be shooed out of the slot.

choices.label: Splash it out of the slot

encounter_drake.narration: The young drake rears up and slaps the stream, and the whole slot becomes a splash fight. Move it along before the next climbers get soaked.

scene_drake_shooed.narration: The drake squeaks, flops over the rocks and slides into a deep pool beside the path, where it blows a sulky bubble. Then it coughs up a smooth blue charm it has been keeping under its tongue, and pushes it across the stones with its nose. "Thanks," says its bubble. The slot is open, and the next climbers can come up dry.

choices.label: Climb on, with the charm

scene_drake_splashed.narration: The waves are too many, and you are washed back down the stones in a heap. The path-keeper has heard the splashing. He comes down the path with a stack of towels and a tea tray, and bangs the tray like a gong until the drake slides into a far pool and sulks. He wraps everybody up and hands out hot tea. Nobody gets a charm tonight, but the slot is clear.

choices.label: Climb on, warm and dry

interaction_camp.narration: The flat rock at the edge of the foothills is bare and a little cold, and the sun is nearly gone. A camp will not make itself. Everybody does a piece of it.

interaction.cue: Everybody add something to the camp until it feels cozy.

options.label: Light a little fire
options.reaction: A small flame crackles on the rock.

options.label: Roll out the blankets
options.reaction: The blankets go down in a soft row.

options.label: Warm the moss tea
options.reaction: Tea steam curls up into the dusk.

stages: The fire settles down to a glow.

onSuccess.narration: The fire glows, the blankets are warm, and the tea tastes like a rainy afternoon, in a good way.

onFailure.narration: The fire is a little smoky and the blankets are a little crooked, but the camp will do.

voiceGuide.tone: cozy, wise and quietly amazed; a town of librarians who are also a forest, with the mountain grumbling at the edge
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.door_archivist: brisk bigfoot archivist; fussy about feet, warm once she decides you matter
npcVoices.oldest_archivist: very old, very slow, a bird lives in his beard; talks to the knot-cords as much as to you
npcVoices.eldest: MossHome elder; mild, sips tea between every sentence, asks to be told second and means it
npcVoices.runner: a MossHome runner; cheerful, out of breath, never stops jogging even while talking
npcVoices.soup_woman: a Deep Hollow Cult member; genuinely kind, soft-spoken, believes every word; kindness first, always, and never menacing
npcVoices.flood_warden: MossHome bigfoot in very tall boots; brisk, practical, has seen every kind of soggy
npcVoices.path_keeper: old bigfoot who keeps the halfway hut on the high paths; slow, kind, proud of his visitors' book
npcVoices.young_gatherer: a young dragonling gatherer; insists she is not lost, knows the one rule by heart, braver than she feels
